definitions.explanation: A practice exercise in which people rehearse evacuating a building or area safely in case of fire, earthquake, or other emergency. Routinely conducted at schools, workplaces, and public facilities.

examples.japanese: {学校|がっこう}で{避難訓練|ひなんくんれん}があった。
examples.english: There was an evacuation drill at school.

examples.japanese: {地震|じしん}を{想定|そうてい}した{避難訓練|ひなんくんれん}に{参加|さんか}した。
examples.english: I took part in an evacuation drill that assumed an earthquake.

examples.japanese: {毎年|まいとし}、{会社|かいしゃ}では{火災|かさい}を{想定|そうてい}した{避難訓練|ひなんくんれん}を{行|おこな}っている。
examples.english: Every year, our company conducts an evacuation drill that assumes a fire.

notes:
Compound of {避難|ひなん} (evacuation, taking refuge) + {訓練|くんれん} (training, drill).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {避難訓練|ひなんくんれん}を{行|おこな}う: to conduct an evacuation drill
- {避難訓練|ひなんくんれん}に{参加|さんか}する: to take part in a drill
- {火災|かさい}{避難訓練|ひなんくんれん}: fire evacuation drill

CULTURAL CONTEXT: Given Japan's frequent earthquakes and strong fire-safety culture, regular {避難訓練|ひなんくんれん} are a routine part of school and workplace life.
